articles.title: Wrexham and Rochdale train services rejected over west coast line pressure
articles.summary: Regulator also vetoes extra Blackpool service, saying insufficient space for new direct trains to London

blocks.text: Plans to run direct train services to Wrexham and Rochdale from London have been rejected by the rail regulator because of “significant pressure” on the line.
The Office of Rail and Road said that there was insufficient space on the crowded west coast main line to introduce the two new separate train services.
It also vetoed plans for additional London-Blackpool train services wanted by Avanti.

The ORR had last year knocked back plans for a new independent open access service linking Wrexham and the capital put forward by the Wrexham, Shropshire & Midlands Railway Company (WSMR). WSMR had submitted plans for a slightly less frequent service but the ORR said the new routes would still put the reliability of the wider railway at risk.
The new service could have allowed Wrexham to capitalise further on the town’s Hollywood-meets-football mini-boom, fuelled by the Wrexham AFC co-owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney.
Proposals for a new Lumo service between London and Rochdale, again slimmed down after being rejected in 2025, were once more rebuffed.

The ORR also said Avanti could not add more Blackpool services from London. However, it did approve one extra London-Chester evening service from Avanti, which would otherwise have run as a “ghost train”, with crew and the rolling stock returning north to the depot overnight. The decision follows the outcry over the ORR’s initial ruling on a Manchester-London service which was barred from taking passengers last year.

The regulator said its assessment, backed by external reviews, was that the “capacity and performance of the southern section of the west coast main line has not materially changed since similar applications were rejected in 2025”.
It said gaps in the current timetable were needed to provide important space for trains to recover when things went wrong, rather than escalating chaos.

Stephanie Tobyn, ORR’s director of strategy, policy and reform, said: “New services, destinations and greater choice can bring real benefits for passengers and communities. But the west coast main line is already under significant pressure, with performance reflecting limited resilience on a heavily used part of the rail network.
after newsletter promotion

“Our detailed analysis has shown that adding more trains to the current timetable would reduce the ability to recover when disruption occurs, increasing the risk of delays spreading and making reliability of the network worse for all passengers.”

Private operators such as First Group, owners of Lumo, have been looking to increase open-access routes – such as Hull Trains and Grand Central – as Labour has renationalised major rail contracts in the transition to Great British Railways.
London-Wrexham direct trains briefly ran from London Marylebone from 2008 to 2011 as an open-access service but stopped owing to financial losses.

articles.title: BIR: Sara Duterte received income from Davao City in 2023 when she was VP
articles.summary: The Constitution prohibits the Vice President from receiving any other emolument from the government

blocks.text: Bureau of Internal Revenue Office of the Commissioner chief of staff Ann Garcia-Marquez takes the witness stand in Vice President Sara Duterte's trial on October 8, 2026.
Rappler screenshot
The Constitution prohibits the Vice President from receiving any other emolument from the government

MANILA, Philippines – Records of the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) show that Vice President Sara Duterte received income from Davao City Hall in 2023, when she was already the country’s second highest official, potentially in violation of the Constitution.

At the Vice President’s impeachment trial on Thursday, October 8, BIR Office of the Commissioner chief of staff Anne Loraine Garcia-Marquez confirmed that Duterte signed a BIR 2316 Form with the Davao City government, listed as employer back in 2023.
“VP Sara Duterte received compensation income from the city government of Davao in 2023,” Garcia-Marquez told the impeachment court.
The witness did not disclose the actual amount.

blocks.caption: BIR: Sara Duterte received income from Davao City in 2023 when she was VP

blocks.text: Duterte’s brother Sebastian has been Davao City mayor since 2022.
Article VII, Section 6 of the Constitution states that the President and the Vice President “shall not receive during their tenure any other emolument from the Government or any other source.”
Article VII, Section 13 also prohibits the Vice President from practicing any other profession during one’s tenure.

The direct examination of the BIR witness by prosecutor Erwin Matib is part of the prosecution’s bigger case of Duterte’s alleged unexplained wealth. The prosecution alleged that this is tantamount to betrayal of public trust and culpable violation of the Constitution.
Garcia-Marquez’s testimony also established that Duterte and her husband, Manases “Mans” Carpio, registered a net income of only P85.34 million after taxes from 2027 to 2025.
“This cannot explain the increase in her net worth, which reached P98 million as of VP Sara’s latest SALN,” Matib said. – Rappler.com

articles.title: German Bundeswehr: A new naval port in Emden
articles.summary: Citing the escalating security threat, the German Navy has decided to establish a second port on the North Sea coast. Emden was chosen as the location.

image.caption: Emden on the North Sea will be a naval city againImage: Sina Schuldt/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: After months of evaluating different locations, the German Minister of Defense Boris Pistorius has now announced that the Bundeswehr's new naval port will be built in Emden on the North Sea coast of Lower Saxony. "Emden offers ideal conditions, such as quick access to the Atlantic Ocean and the far north," the defense minister explained, elaborating on the choice. He noted that a new port is needed to accommodate the growing German Navy: new ships and boats require berths, and additional service members need housing. Furthermore, he said, "This will enhance the deterrence capabilities of both Germany and NATO."

The commercial port of Emden is the economic heart of East Frisia. Not only does it dominate the cityscape, but it also provides thousands of jobs. Directly adjacent to the port is the large Volkswagen plant, from which cars are exported by ship to destinations around the world. The port also serves as a shipment hub for large components for wind farms in the North Sea. Now, a naval base with up to 2,000 military posts will be built by the early 2030s. Emden hosted a Bundeswehr base until 1997, but it was no longer needed after the end of the Cold War and was consequently decommissioned.

blocks.caption: Defense Minister Boris Pistorius announced the plans for a new naval port in EmdenImage: Sina Schuldt/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Large open spaces are available

According to experts, there are a number of reasons why Emden is a good location. While finding land on the coast to build on is tough, that's not the case in Emden. The port city has "the great advantage of having a lot of available space where a new port can be developed," says Johannes Peters, an expert on maritime security at the Institute for Security Policy at the University of Kiel. "Emden offers the opportunity to build a dedicated naval port that complies with the latest requirements, including those for security and port protection," Peters emphasizes in an interview with DW. Pistorius estimates that up to 450 hectares of land will be needed — equivalent to about 630 soccer fields.

The only naval port currently on the German North Sea coast is located in Wilhelmshaven. From a strategic perspective, it doesn't make sense to have just one port and nothing to fall back on, security expert Peters emphasized. "If some kind of scenario where conflict breaks out were to actually occur and this infrastructure were to fail, then you'd have a real problem. That's why they want to diversify their options here now."

Defense Minister Boris Pistorius also emphasized the strategic advantage of a second naval port on the North Sea: "This makes us harder to predict in an emergency and expands our operational capabilities."
Relief for Wilhelmshaven

The planned port in Emden is intended to complement and provide relief for the Wilhelmshaven naval base. This is where Operational Flotilla 2 is stationed, a large formation consisting of frigates and supply ships. The Wilhelmshaven naval base is also being expanded as the fleet grows and personnel levels increase.

In reference to Wilhelmshaven, the defense minister said that the "smallest navy in the history of the Bundeswehr" currently has more responsibilities than ever before. "So the navy must grow, and it will. We have laid the groundwork for this in all areas.
German rearmament sparks controversy, again
Bremerhaven to become a NATO hub

Bremerhaven was also on the shortlist. Although it will not be getting a naval base, the German government is investing a great deal of money there as well. The port will be expanded into a logistical hub that could be used to deploy large troop contingents and heavy equipment from NATO allies in the event of an emergency. That is the plan outlined in "Operation Plan Germany," Germany's defense plan in the event of a crisis or threat to alliance security. The federal government is allocating up to €1.35 billion ($1.51 billion) for the expansion.
New jobs for Emden

Although Emden has been officially chosen as the site, so far this is only a memorandum of understanding between the Ministry of Defense, the state of Lower Saxony and the city of Emden. Construction of the naval port is likely to take years. "There are still major hurdles to overcome," says Defense Minister Pistorius.
"You can't just walk into a home improvement store and buy a new naval base. Marine engineering, transportation links, the barracks — we need to get started on these right away."

The city, with its approximately 50,000 residents, is expected to benefit from the construction of the port, especially since the future of the local Volkswagen plant is uncertain because of ongoing economic trouble for the automaker. Mayor Tim Kruithoff was all the more delighted: "This is a great day for Emden." He described the planned naval base as "an extraordinary opportunity" for jobs and for the economic development of the entire region.
This article was originally written in German.

articles.title: Senate OKs bill banning those below 18 years old from social media
articles.summary: Senator Risa Hontiveros offers the only ‘no’ vote, suggesting tiered access by age instead

blocks.text: SOCIAL MEDIA. Instagram, TikTok, Snapchat, YouTube, Facebook, Twitch and Reddit applications are displayed on a mobile phone ahead of new law banning social media for users under 16 in Australia, in this picture illustration taken on December 9, 2025.
Hollie Adams/Reuters
Senator Risa Hontiveros offers the only ‘no’ vote, suggesting tiered access by age instead

MANILA, Philippines – The Senate on Thursday, October 8, passed Senate Bill No. 2424 or the Safe Media Access and Responsible Technology for Kids in Digital Spaces (SMART KIDS) Act that seeks to restrict anyone under 18 years old from accessing social media or other “high-risk digital services.”

The bill, sponsored by Senator Robin Padilla, compels the suspension, restriction, disabling or removal of any account that has been reasonably determined as being owned or used by a minor. It will also prevent minors from creating accounts, with platforms required to have effective age-assurance measures.
The approved version of the bill increased the scope of the restrictions to cover those under 18 years old, up from the original version’s proposed 16-year-old threshold.

The Senate’s debate over social media regulation for the youth vacillated between an outright ban versus a tiered “age-appropriate” framework, which would offer different levels of restrictions by age. The former appeared to have won that debate, with the country facing a spate of deadly school shootings and other violent incidents, attributed partly to certain influences within online environments or effects of social media use to young users.
Of the 17 senators who voted, Risa Hontiveros was the lone dissenting vote.

Hontiveros explained her vote in a Facebook post, citing some examples about how young Filipinos can use social media platforms to voice out abuses, to connect with family living abroad, or to do a side hustle.

She said: “Social media has become a space where young people build and maintain their connections with their friends, communities, families, and loved ones. An outright ban strips away these very connections that have become so important in their day-to-day lives.”

She said that a complete ban for all individuals under 18 years old fails to take into consideration that, for example, a 13-year-old and a 15-year-old have different levels of development. A tiered implementation for social media access may be more apt, Hontiveros argued.

“For younger adolescents, we should require stronger default privacy and data settings, tighter restrictions on adult contact, limits on targeted advertising and profiling, and stronger parental and educational safeguards. As adolescents mature, maaari natin silang unti-unting bigyan ng awtonomiya habang nananatili ang mga proteksyon laban sa abuso at eksploytasyon, at harmful content,” she said. (As adolescents mature, we can slowly give them autonomy while protections remain from abuse, exploitation and harmful content.)

Senator Hontiveros authored the SAGIP BATA Act, which criminalizes the “sadistic extortion” of children or the use of threats, manipulation, blackmail, deception and similar means to compel children into grave, cruel, degrading or harmful acts. It has also been approved by the Senate.
Senator Joel Villanueva welcomed the bill’s passing:

“Bilang mga magulang, ginagawa natin ang lahat upang maging ligtas ang ating mga anak sa bahay at sa paaralan. Dapat umabot ang proteksiyong iyon hanggang sa kanilang mga screen, kung saan nang dahil sa isang click maaari silang malantad sa pambubully, karahasan, at pagsasamantala.”

(As parents, we do everything we can to keep our children safe at home and in school. That protection should extend to their screens, where a single click can expose them to bullying, violence, and exploitation.)
The SMART KIDS Act will now be transmitted to the House for its own review. – Rappler.com

articles.title: SC makes foreign divorce easier for Filipino spouses to prove
articles.summary: The Supreme Court (SC) on Thursday said it has approved amendments to the Rules of Court to make it easier for Filipino spouses to prove a foreign divorce when seeking its recognition in the country.

blocks.text: Published October 8, 2026 5:24pm
The Supreme Court (SC) on Thursday said it has approved amendments to the Rules of Court to make it easier for Filipino spouses to prove a foreign divorce when seeking its recognition in the country.
According to the SC, Filipino spouses seeking recognition of their divorce under Article 26(2) of the Family Code will no longer need to prove the applicable foreign law.
It said that spouses will only need to prove that the divorce took place.
“The SC recognized that proving foreign law under the existing rules can be difficult for Filipino spouses, particularly overseas Filipino workers,” it said.

It said that consultations of its sub-technical working group with the Department of Foreign Affairs with the Department of Foreign Affairs revealed that foreign family laws are difficult to obtain as they are often spread across different jurisdictions.
The High Court added that some countries do not have officials who can certify the laws while some do not provide English translations.
“Through these amendments, the SC aims to remove unnecessary barriers and make it easier for Filipinos to exercise their rights under the law,” it said.
According to the SC, the amendments will take effect 15 days after they are posted on the court’s website.

“The amendments introduce Section 48-A of Rule 39, which presumes that a foreign divorce between a Filipino and a foreign spouse allows the foreign spouse to remarry under foreign law, unless the divorce decree itself states that it is only a limited divorce,” it said.
The SC said that the party opposing the petition for recognition will now bear the burden of proving that the divorce is not absolute.
Further, the SC said that the rule presumes that an English translation of the foreign divorce document is accurate if the translator certifies its accuracy under oath.
“These presumptions are disputable, meaning they may be challenged with contrary evidence, under Section 3 of Rule 131,” it said.
According to the SC, individuals seeking to challenge the presumptions may submit a certified true copy of the applicable foreign divorce law, including
its English translation, obtained from the Office of the Court Administrator (OCA).
Meanwhile, the SC stressed that a petition for judicial recognition is still required while the substantive requirements remain the same.
“Recognition of a foreign divorce may still be opposed on grounds such as of jurisdiction, lack of notice, fraud, or a clear mistake of law or fact,” it said. —NB, GMA News

articles.title: Philippines, France boosts agricultural ties after high-level meetings in Paris
articles.summary: The Philippines and France are seeking to beef up their cooperation in the agricultural sector following recent high-level meetings in Paris on September 23 to 24, the Department of Agriculture (DA)…

blocks.text: Published October 8, 2026 5:06pm

The Philippines and France are seeking to beef up their cooperation in the agricultural sector following recent high-level meetings in Paris on September 23 to 24, the Department of Agriculture (DA) said.

Agricultural Secretary Francisco Tiu Laurel Jr. said the enhanced ties mean "greater opportunities to bring in technology, knowledge and investments that can benefit our farmers and strengthen our food systems."
“Our partnership with France is important as we work to make Philippine agriculture more productive, competitive and resilient," Tiu Laurel said.

During the 4th Philippines-France Joint Steering Committee (JSC), stakeholders identified animal health, food safety, dairy development, geographical indications, organic agriculture, development financing, and agricultural research and innovation as priority areas for closer cooperation.
Manila and France also explored deeper collaboration with the French Agricultural Research Centre for International Development (CIRAD).

According to DA, this joint effort will focus on research, graduate studies, scientific exchanges, and researcher mobility, targeting key sectors like mango and banana farming, aquaculture, agroecology, climate resilience, sustainable landscapes, and modern agritech.
France also expressed support for training Filipino veterinarians in biosecurity, transboundary animal disease control, border controls, and risk-based inspection.
Meanwhile, during the Agriculture and the 3rd Philippines-France Agricultural Forum, France shared its experience with using advanced agricultural machinery and standards.

The Philippine delegation led by DA Assistant Secretary Paz Benavidez II also met with the Agence Française de Développement (AFD) to explore possible support for climate-resilient agriculture, research and innovation, geographical indications, organic agriculture, and the marine and blue economy. —Vince Angelo Ferreras/NB, GMA News

articles.title: Covid, Brexit and Liz Truss mini-budget led to lasting decline in mental health, study finds
articles.summary:
Researchers found five events, including Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, caused serious damage to mental wellbeing across UK

Brexit, Liz Truss’s mini-budget and other “shocks” over the last 10…

blocks.text: Brexit, Liz Truss’s mini-budget and other “shocks” over the last 10 years have led to a serious and lasting deterioration in the UK population’s mental health, research has found.
Russia’s invasion of Ukraine and the first and second Covid lockdowns also triggered big rises in psychological distress, as measured by the number of people with depression and anxiety.

The findings come as Prof Peter Fonagy prepares to publish the report of his long-waited government-commissioned inquiry into the dramatic increases in recent years in diagnoses of mental illness, ADHD and autism. It will be published on Friday amid concern that those conditions help explain why a record 2.8 million Britons are too sick to work and almost 1 million young people aged 16 to 24 have become “Neets” – not in education, employment or training.

Researchers led by Dr Annie Jeffery of University College London used data from the UK Household Longitudinal Study of 87,857 people aged 16 and older, which was collected every year between 2009 and 2024, to estimate the mental health impact of those five “systemic shocks”.
“The past decade or so has been tumultuous, shaped by multiple overlapping shocks and ongoing uncertainty and instability that have impacted mental health in Britain,” said Jeffery.
“We have shown that major government decisions and current global events can have substantial impacts on people’s mental health.”

All five events caused immediate and serious damage to overall mental wellbeing across the UK. But the Brexit referendum in June 2016 and first pandemic lockdown in March 2020 caused the most damage, the research team found.

Their analysis of the general health questionnaire’s GHQ-12 screening tool, which measures mental health, found that the UK’s vote to leave the European Union led to an increase in overall mental ill-health equivalent to about 120,000 more people overall seeking a GP’s help for depression.

However, the first Covid lockdown, when the then prime minister, Boris Johnson, told people to “stay at home”, had a much larger impact, as measured by a much bigger rise in the UK’s GHQ-12 score. That jump equated to about 900,000 more people in total visiting a family doctor because they had developed symptoms of depression, Jeffery said.

Russia’s offensive against Ukraine in February 2022 led to about 15,000 more Britons a month seeking a GP’s help for depression. After Liz Truss’s mini-budget in September 2022, which proved disastrous for the UK economy, about 23,000 more people a month visited their family doctor’s surgery because they were depressed.

“We observed increased psychological distress immediately after the Brexit referendum and the first Covid-19 lockdown, with more insidious monthly increases in psychological distress after the Russian invasion of Ukraine and the 2022 mini-budget,” said Jeffrey.

Andy Bell, the chief executive of the Centre for Mental Health thinktank, said: “There is clear evidence that Covid had a big impact on mental health. And it makes sense that the other ‘shocks’ listed here would do so, either directly, by making people feel less secure and less connected, or as after-effects, for example the cost of living crisis.

“It’s also clear that rising distress in the population is not due to a single cause but the effect of all these things added together, made worse by years of austerity giving fewer buffers against ‘shocks’ like this.”
Mental ill-health costs the UK £300bn a year, according to research by the thinktank.

The UCL-led team’s findings have been published in the journal BMJ Mental Health. They found that psychological distress had been increasing in the UK from 2009 to a degree that was clinically significant but accelerated from 2015 onwards. Even though the most recent of the five events occurred in 2022, the heightened distress in the population that followed them has persisted and not gone back to the much lower levels seen before 2016, they found.

The total number of people in England in contact with NHS mental health services almost doubled from 2.64 million in 2016-17 to 4.13 million in 2024-25. The number of new referrals the NHS receives every month for mental ill-health has jumped from 360,000 in April 2022 to 530,000 in July 2026 – a jump of 47%.

The huge rise in demand for care – driven by “shocks” causing anxiety, stress and worry – has left NHS services struggling “as more people than ever are reaching out for support”, said Tom Pollard, the mental health charity Mind’s director of policy, campaigns and public affairs.

articles.title: NASA Apollo program pioneer Margaret Hamilton dies
articles.summary: US scientist Margaret Hamilton is being hailed as a pioneer for her groundbreaking work developing software for NASA's Apollo lunar program. She died at the age of 90.

image.caption: Margaret Hamilton, pictured in 1969, headed a group that programmed the computers used in NASA's moon landingImage: AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Software engineer Margaret Hamilton, who led the team that programmed the first computers used by NASA's Apollo mission to land humans on the moon, has died at the age of 90.
Her death on September 30 was announced Wednesday by the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), where she worked from 1959 to the mid-70s.
The university described her as profoundly influential in the field of software development, saying she had "forged new paths in computer science and engineering."
NASA chief Jared Isaacmen paid tribute on X, calling Hamilton "a pioneer whose work helped make Apollo and humanity's first journeys to the moon possible."
How did Hamilton come to work on the lunar program?
Hamilton studied mathematics before moving to Boston, Massachusetts, in 1959.
She began working at MIT soon afterwards, and in 1965 applied to join a lab at the university that was seeking people to develop software to "send a man to the moon."
The lab had won a contract from NASA to build the onboard flight software for the Apollo program.

blocks.caption: 'Looking back, we were the luckiest people in the world,' Hamilton said of her time working for the Apollo missionImage: Wikipedia

blocks.text: Hamilton was hired as the first programmer for the project, MIT said, adding that she was also the project's first female programmer.
She initially worked on the first software for the uncrewed Apollo missions, before being promoted to lead the team developing on-board flight software for the crewed missions.
"By 1968, she was assistant director in charge of (Apollo's) Command and Service Module team, and more than 400 people were working on Apollo's software," MIT said.

"To say Margaret Hamilton was a pioneer — to say she was ahead of her time — would be a dramatic understatement," said Olivier de Weck, the Apollo Program Professor and interim head of the MIT Department Aeronautics and Astronautics.

"She was a software engineer at a time when that field was in its infancy, and she not only developed advanced code herself but also led a team in using that nascent technology to develop one of the most complex systems humanity had ever achieved," de Weck added.

blocks.caption: Hamilton's achievements were recognized in 2016 when then US President Barack Obama awarded her the Presidential Medal of FreedomImage: ZUMA/IMAGO

blocks.text: 'There was no second chance'

Speaking of her time working on the Apollo program, Hamilton told MIT News in 2009: "There was no second chance. We knew that. We took our work seriously, many of us beginning this journey while still in our 20s."

"Coming up with solutions and new ideas was an adventure. Dedication and commitment were a given," she added. "Because software was a mystery, a black box, upper management gave us total freedom and trust."
"Looking back, we were the luckiest people in the world; there was no choice but to be pioneers."
Hamilton published more than 130 papers and went on to start her own software companies Higher Order Software and Hamilton Technologies.

In 2016, she was awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom by former US President Barack Obama, whose citation said: "Hamilton defined new forms of software engineering and helped launch an industry that would forever change human history. Her software architecture led to giant leaps for humankind, writing the code that helped America set foot on the moon.”

articles.title: Polls open in Holborn and St Pancras byelection – UK politics live
articles.summary:
Voters choosing replacement for Keir Starmer, who announced he was standing down last month

The French finance minister, Roland Lescure, said the UK could rejoin the EU…

blocks.text: Key events

items: 25m agoVoters go to the polls in Holborn and St Pancras byelection

blocks.text: The French finance minister, Roland Lescure, said the UK could rejoin the EU “anytime” after Andy Burnham indicated a major review of Britain’s relationship with the bloc.
Lescure said it was up to the British public whether to return to the EU, telling the BBC that “if they’re willing to come back, they will have to decide”.
“But what I can tell them is: come back, anytime,” he added. Ben Quinn has the full report here.

blocks.caption: France’s finance minister Roland Lescure said the UK should rejoin the EU ‘anytime’. Photograph: Kenzo Tribouillard/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: As our political correspondent Aletha Adu reported last week, the prime minister opened the door to the UK rejoining the EU, saying Britain could “go all the way” as he prepares to reconsider Labour’s post-Brexit red lines.
Voters go to the polls in Holborn and St Pancras byelection
Good morning and welcome to our UK politics live blog.
Polls have opened in Keir Starmer’s old seat in Holborn and St Pancras, where the Green party leader, Zack Polanski, is hoping to break Labour’s longstanding grip in the north London constituency.

blocks.caption: A dog is led towards a polling station as voting begins in the Holborn and St Pancras byelection. Photograph: Leon Neal/Getty Images

blocks.text: He might have his work cut out for him. Labour’s Sagal Abdi-Wali is projected to retain the seat in today’s byelection, but the party shouldn’t take victory for granted. As the Guardian’s senior political correspondent, Peter Walker, reports, Polanski has mounted an intensive campaign, but the scale of the challenge is clear from the numbers. Starmer won the seat by 11,500 votes in 2024, after Labour majorities of nearly 28,000 in 2019 and more than 30,500 in 2017.
You can read Peter’s report from this morning here:
In other news:

On the agenda is a new joint security partnership to counter sabotage, cyber-attacks and other hybrid threats, as well as support for Ukraine, instability in the Middle East, and disruption to global trade routes. articles.title: South China Sea? We refer to it as West Philippine Sea --Marcos
articles.summary: President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. on Thursday said that Manila calls the disputed waters “West Philippine Sea”, not the South China Sea.

blocks.text: Published October 8, 2026 4:49pm
President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. on Thursday said that Manila calls the disputed waters “West Philippine Sea”, not the South China Sea.

During the Forbes Global CEO Conference in Singapore, Marcos spoke about the country’s ongoing efforts to exert its sovereignty in the disputed waters. He explained the Filipinos’ use of the term ‘West Philippine Sea’ to the business leaders in the audience.
“The challenges that we are facing now in the South China Sea, we refer to it as the West Philippine Sea,” Marcos said.
“That’s a good name change,” Forbes Editor-in-Chief Steve Forbes said in reply.

“Well, because part of the claim was, look, it’s called China, so South China Seas, it must belong to China. And so we thought, well, you know, it’s been on the… western side of the Philippines, you know, since time immemorial. So we call it the West Philippine Sea,” Marcos said.
West Philippine Sea vs. South China Sea
Government agencies began using the term “West Philippine Sea” following Administrative Order No. 29, which was issued by the late president Benigno Aquino III in 2012.

Under the order, the National Mapping and Resource Information Authority was ordered to publish maps and charts with the term “West Philippine Sea” for western maritime areas within the Philippines’ 200 nautical mile exclusive economic zone (EEZ).

All other government agencies were ordered to adopt the name, with the Department of Foreign Affairs also being instructed to inform the United Nations and other international organizations of the new map.
However, the West Philippine Sea solely refers to the waters within the Philippines’ EEZ. The West Philippine Sea is a part of the larger South China Sea, according to the Naitonal Maritime Council.
Beijing has laid claim to most of the South China Sea, including areas within the Philippine EEZ.
While the Permanent Court of Arbitration’s decision upheld the Philippines’ EEZ in 2016, China has continuously disregarded this and laid claim to most of the West Philippine Sea. —RF, GMA News

articles.title: Oil prices rise sharply on Middle East tensions and US hurricane threat
articles.summary: Global bond market sell-off continues and stocks fall amid another wave of potential strikes against Iran

blocks.text: Oil prices have risen sharply amid fears about escalating tensions in the Middle East and a squeeze on production from the threat of a hurricane off the US coast.
Brent crude, the international benchmark, rose by 3.8% to $104 a barrel on Thursday, triggering a wave of selling in the global bond and stock markets.

The White House has asked the Pentagon to draw up options for strikes against Iran before the US midterm elections, according to a report in The Atlantic. The report cited unnamed officials in Donald Trump’s administration who said the size and targets of potential strikes, and whether they will go ahead, are still being debated.

The report has weakened hopes that Trump will refrain from escalating the conflict with Iran before the midterm polls next month. A “limited operation” could be followed up by more substantial action after the midterms, it states.

Another wave of strikes against Iran represents further risk to oil supply from the Middle East, with the US-Israeli war against Tehran now entering its eighth month. Attacks on tankers in the strait of Hormuz reached their highest levels of ⁠the war, ⁠cutting ​traffic through the waterway and deepening fears about supply.
The latest attack came ⁠on Wednesday, when a tanker was hit by multiple projectiles off the north coast of Qatar, causing casualties, according to ​the United Kingdom Maritime ‌Trade Operations.
Oil prices also rose in response to a squeeze on production in the Gulf of Mexico, after the tropical storm Isaias strengthened to become the first hurricane of the Atlantic season.
Shell and Chevron both said they were shutting down production as the storm approached the region, forecast to make landfall on Friday or Saturday.

Maersk, the Danish shipping group, added to worries around rising energy prices on Thursday after it said it was increasing its emergency fuel surcharge on all its export collections and import deliveries. The rise in energy prices has fed fears about inflation, reinforcing expectations that central banks will have to raise their interest rates in order to control rising prices.

A sell-off in global bond markets continued on Thursday. In France, which has been hit particularly hard over worries around its rising debt and growing spending, the 10-year yield rose by 6 basis points to 4.931%, just behind the 24-year high of 4.994% it hit last week. Yields rise when prices fall.
The German 10-year yield, the benchmark for European debt, rose by 2 basis points to 3.504%.
after newsletter promotion
The yield on the US 10-year treasury, which is widely considered the best quality government debt on the market, rose by 5 basis points to 5.331%.
Global stocks also fell, with Japan’s Nikkei share index falling 1.4% and the South Korean Kospi down 2.6%.
In Europe, the Stoxx Europe 600, which tracks the biggest companies on the continent, dropped 1%. The UK’s FTSE 100 slipped by 0.6% in early trading on Thursday.

articles.title: Alan Cayetano wishes Mark Villar well after transferring to majority
articles.summary: Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano on Thursday said the minority bloc will continue “to stand for what is right,” following the surprise move of Senator Mark Villar to transfer to the…

blocks.text: Published October 8, 2026 4:43pm

Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano on Thursday said the minority bloc will continue “to stand for what is right,” following the surprise move of Senator Mark Villar to transfer to the majority.
In a statement, Cayetano said he understands “all too well” the circumstances and considerations that lead to changes in political alliances.
“Senate coalitions may change, but our vision, principles, and commitment to God and to the Filipino people remain steadfast,” he said.

“As we continue to pray for our country, we wish Senator Mark Villar and all our colleagues well. May God grant us all the wisdom, humility, and strength to faithfully serve Him and the Filipino people,” he added.
Cayetano said the minority bloc “will continue to fulfill its responsibilities as fiscalizers and constructive oppositionists,” who would uphold the rights of every Filipino.

“Since May 11, it has become increasingly clear how important it is for this administration to maintain a closely allied working majority in the Senate. But regardless of how the political landscape shifts, our duty remains unchanged. We will continue to stand for what is right, uphold our institutions, and work for the good of our nation,” he said.

On May 11, a leadership coup happened in the Senate after Senator Ronald “Bato” Dela Rosa suddenly reappeared during the session, resulting in the ouster of then-Senate President Vicente “Tito” Sotto III and the election of Cayetano to the top Senate post.
Cayetano was replaced by incumbent Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian a month after.
Senator Bong Go, a member of the minority bloc, said he respects the decision of Villar to join the majority, affirming that they remain on good terms.
“Gano’n naman po talaga dito sa Senado. We respect each other kung ano magiging decision nila,” Go said.
(That’s really how it is here in the Senate. We respect each other regarding whatever decision we make.)
Robin Padilla, also a minority senator, said there is no need for a “big reaction” from the minority as Villar was a previous member of the majority.
Implications to impeachment?

Senate Majority Leader Juan Miguel “Migz” Zubiri, meanwhile, believes that the move of Villar had nothing to do with the conviction vote threshold in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.

“No, nothing to do whatsoever. You know, being a member of the majority, doesn't automatically mean that you will vote for conviction or for acquittal. Hindi po ibig sabihin ‘yun. Baka may members kami sa majority, biglang mag-vote for acquittal din at baka may members din ng minority that will vote for conviction. It all has to do with evidence presented,” Zubiri explained.

(No, nothing to do whatsoever. You know, being a member of the majority, doesn't automatically mean that you will vote for conviction or for acquittal. It doesn't mean like that. Maybe we have members in the majority who will suddenly vote for acquittal, and maybe there are also members of the minority who will vote for conviction. It all has to do with evidence presented.)
Zubiri also distanced the majority bloc from the move of Villar to vote in favor of appealing the decision on the original 16-vote threshold to convict Duterte.
“We had nothing to do with that. That's a conscience vote,” he said.
The majority leader also said that Villar chose to transfer from the minority on his own.
“Siya nakiusap sa amin na sama na lang siya sa (he was the one who asked to join us)…he wants to join the majority to be more productive and so we welcome that,” Zubiri added. — RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: Marcos shares greatest fear on West Philippine Sea in Forbes forum
articles.summary: President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. on Thursday shared that his greatest fear in the West Philippine Sea is a soldier making a mistake that turns into "something out of control."
articles.byline: JONATHAN ANDAL, JEAN MANGALUZ, GMA News

blocks.text: Published October 8, 2026 4:38pm
President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. on Thursday shared that his greatest fear in the West Philippine Sea is a soldier making a mistake that turns into "something out of control."
Speaking before foreign business leaders at the Forbes Global CEO Conference in Singapore, Marcos said this was the reason why the Code of Conduct in the said waters was crucial.

“My greatest fear is that some seaman, some soldier, just makes a mistake. And that mistake turns into something that goes out of control. And that’s why the Code of Conduct is very, very important, and we’re working very, very hard. We’re making good progress, as a matter of fact, in terms of the Code of Conduct,” Marcos said.
"I don't know if we can find a resolution to the problem, but we are resigned to just being able to manage the problem so that we do not have mistakes, we don't have misinterpretations,” he added.
Marcos said that he was uncertain if the territorial row could be resolved, but said that it had to be managed. While discussions over the Code of Conduct have been long, Marcos remained optimistic.
“We are determined to come to an agreement and to hopefully de-escalate the situation,” Marcos said.

During the forum, Marcos also reiterated Manila’s claim over the West Philippine Sea, saying that it was his and every Filipino’s duty to protect the country’s territory. He said that in the view of international law, particularly the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, the disputed waters belong to the Philippines.
“It is very, very clear that these areas are part of Philippine sovereign territory, and also part of our economic zone," Marcos said.

"And therefore it is imperative on us; I took an oath to defend the constitution of the Philippines, when I took on—every office that I took on—I took that oath, that I will support and defend the constitution of the Philippines, and the constitution of the Philippines defines the territory, the sovereign territory of the Philippines such,” he added.
“That is my duty to do that as president; it is the duty, in my view, of every Philippine citizen to do that same, and that’s what we're trying to do,” he added.

The President’s first activity in Singapore was his attendance at the Forbes Global CEO Conference, where he served as the guest speaker. Marcos addressed 470 business leaders, encouraging them to invest in the Philippines.

China has continuously claimed most of the West Philippine Sea for itself, despite the 2016 Permanent Court of Arbitration decision that ruled in favor of the Philippines’ claim over its own exclusive economic zone.
Manila’s relationship with Beijing has grown colder under Marcos’ administration, with several confrontations in the West Philippine Sea often leaving Filipino sailors injured.
The Armed Forces of the Philippines reported that in September alone, more than 100 Chinese vessels were roaming around the West Philippine Sea. —NB, GMA News

articles.title: Middle Corridor: Can Bulgaria be a safe gateway for Asian imports to the EU?
articles.summary: The EU wants more trade via the "Middle Corridor," which could bring big benefits for Bulgaria. But Tuesday's drone attacks on commercial ships off the Bulgarian coast is a stark reminder of the…

image.caption: Freight rail cars carrying containers are loaded onto a ferry at the Port of Kuryk in Kazakhstan for transportation across the Caspian Sea. The port is a key hub on the Middle CorridorImage: Jens Büttner/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: On the morning of October 6, drones hit two commercial ships off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast, sinking one of the ships and causing alarm and outrage in both Bulgaria and the EU.
The drone attacks come at a time when the EU is pushing for Bulgaria to become a key entry point for goods imported from Asia to the bloc via the trade route known as the Middle Corridor.

The Middle Corridor — which the EU also refers to as the Trans-Caspian Transport Corridor — connects Europe and Asia. It begins in China and runs through Kazakhstan, Azerbaijan, Georgia and Turkey before reaching the EU.
Although it is mostly made up of railways and roads, short sections of the corridor cross the Black Sea and Caspian Sea.
Bulgaria and the Middle Corridor
The EU has this year declared its intention to bet big on this trade route, a move that could have consequences for Bulgaria's railways, roads and ports.
Bulgaria's land border crossing with Turkey, Kapitan Andreevo, is already one of the busiest in Europe. Lines of trucks can frequently be seen queuing at the checkpoint.
The country also has two strategic ports on the Black Sea — Varna and Burgas — and a new section of a railway line between Istanbul and the Bulgarian border is set to open this fall.
In September, EU Commissioner for Enlargement Marta Kos called Bulgaria "Europe's Connectivity Gateway" due to its strategic location on this route.
Wars have disrupted global trade routes

A few months earlier, Kos said that the Middle Corridor could considerably cut transport times from Asia to Europe from 45 days to just 15 days and is safer than the two traditional routes for goods being transported to Europe from Asia.
One of these was an overland route via the Northern Corridor through Russia. Trade along this route dropped sharply after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
The other route, sometimes referred to as the Ocean Route, sees goods traveling by ship through the Red Sea and the Suez Canal.

But fears of disruption caused by wars and instability in the Middle East mean that many goods are now being shipped all the way around Africa — a journey that takes around 45 days. That results in delays and costs for businesses and consumers alike.

All of this explains why the Middle Corridor suddenly seems so attractive — a fact confirmed by Vessela Tcherneva, deputy director of the European Council on Foreign Relations, who is based in Sofia, Bulgaria.

"The Middle Corridor is a project that basically avoids both war theaters that we have near Europe," Tcherneva told DW. "It avoids the route through Russia, and also it avoids the route through the Middle East."
Is the Middle Corridor a realistic alternative?
As promising as it sounds, a lot needs to change before the Middle Corridor can really compete with the Ocean Route.

"You have, first and foremost, security limitations," said Tcherneva. "The security situation in Central Asia needs to really have improved enough so that one can make long-term plans for constructing big projects."
Tcherneva also stressed that weak institutions and bureaucracies in countries along the Middle Corridor are an issue. Russian involvement cannot be ruled out.

"We have seen infrastructure projects in the past not happen because they were not perceived as being in Russia's interest, and the Russians seem to have quite a bit of leverage in the countries along the route," she said, adding that "the outcome of Russia's war in Ukraine is going to have an impact on the success or failure of the Middle Corridor."
Tuesday's drone attacks on commercial ships in the Black Sea are a stark reminder that security on the route could well remain a problem.

In addition, the water level in the Caspian Sea, which is situated on the Middle Corridor, is falling, with climate change as a key driver. This means there is no guarantee that ships will be able to cross it in the future.

blocks.caption: EU Commissioner for Enlargement Marta Kos called Bulgaria 'Europe's Connectivity Gateway' due to its strategic location on the Middle CorridorImage: Dursun Aydemir/Anadolu/picture alliance

blocks.text: Then there is the problem of infrastructure: Ports and railways along the route lack capacity for big increases in trade volumes.
Could Bulgaria benefit?
Despite these risks and limitations, the EU clearly wants to see more trade coming through the Middle Corridor, even if it cannot replace existing routes.

In her recent State of the Union speech, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said that the EU wants to improve what it calls "connectivity." It wants to diversify trade routes, increase trade flows and reduce freight transit times.
To do so, it aims to raise €12 billion ($13.5 billion) in public and private investment.
Bulgaria could benefit from this in a number of ways.

"The Bulgarian railways have been underinvested in for many, many years now — for decades. Bulgarian ports would also benefit greatly from investment," Vessela Tcherneva told DW. "Developing better road connections from the Mediterranean up, but also east-west, would help, especially the north of the country, which is currently not very well connected. So, there are clear benefits."

The Office of the Ombudsman on Thursday warned government officials and employees against using fuel allocated for government vehicles for private vehicles amid rising fuel costs.
In a statement, Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla issued the warning citing a recent case involving a former Bohol provincial board member who was dismissed from service for such offense.

“Acts like this destroy the image of government. Ang mga ganitong gawain—kasama na ang mga higop gasolina, pagkarga sa hindi government vehicle, at pamemeke ng mga resibo—ay hindi ipagsasawalang-bahala ng ahensya,” Remulla said.
(Acts like this destroy the image of government. These kinds of acts—including siphoning off gasoline, loading non-government vehicles, and forging receipts—will not be ignored by the agency.)
The Ombudsman said then Bohol Second District Provincial Board Member Vierna Mae Boniel-Maglasang was ordered dismissed from service for two counts of Serious Dishonesty.
She was penalized with all the accessory penalties of cancellation of eligibility, and is barred from taking civil service examinations. Her retirement benefits were also forfeited.
The Ombudsman said Boniel-Maglasang used a total of 100 liters of gasoline in 2024 that had been allocated for a government vehicle but was instead dispensed into private motor vehicles.
The case stemmed from a complaint filed by Bohol Third District Board Member Dionisio Joseph Balite.

In its 13-page decision, the Ombudsman said charging fuel expenses for a vehicle not covered by the authorized government fuel allocation system showed an intent to circumvent accounting and auditing rules.
According to the Ombudsman, the act also indicated an intent to obtain material gain and could constitute graft and corruption. — Joviland Rita/BM, GMA News

articles.title: Senate passes social media ban for children below 16 on final reading
articles.summary: Senators on Thursday approved on third and final reading a measure that would ban social media use among children under 16 in the Philippines.

blocks.text: Published October 8, 2026 4:28pm
Senators on Thursday approved on third and final reading a measure that would ban social media use among children under 16 in the Philippines.
Senate Bill No. 2424 was supported by 16 senators present during the plenary session, with only Senator Risa Hontiveros voting against the measure.

In contrast, the House of Representatives is proposing a lower minimum age for social media access. On Tuesday, congressmen approved House Bill No. 11566, which seeks to bar children below 13 years old from creating or maintaining social media accounts, on second reading.
Under the Senate bill, children below 16 years old would be prohibited from registering for, accessing, operating, maintaining, or creating accounts on age-restricted social media platforms.
Platforms would be required to suspend, restrict, disable, or remove any account reasonably determined to be owned, operated, or used by a child under 16.

Social media platforms would be required to implement reasonable, proportionate, and effective age-verification measures to prevent children below 16 from creating, accessing, maintaining, or using accounts on age-restricted platforms.
Children aged 16 to below 18, meanwhile, may use age-restricted social media platforms provided they comply with age-assurance requirements and applicable child-safety measures.

Children below 16 may be allowed to access age-restricted platforms if they are specifically required for legitimate educational purposes and certified by the Department of Education (DepEd), Commission on Higher Education (CHED), or Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA), as applicable.
Their access, however, would be limited to educational functions and subject to child protection, privacy, and safety safeguards.
Social media platforms and third-party age-assurance providers could face fines of P1 million to P20 million for each violation.
Repeated, willful, or gross violations could result in the suspension, restriction, or revocation of their operations, permits, or access in the Philippines, subject to due process.

Meanwhile, parents or legal guardians who knowingly and willfully help children below 16 circumvent age-assurance measures, create or obtain accounts for them, or repeatedly violate their obligations through gross negligence could face fines ranging from P5,000 to P50,000 and/or mandatory digital parenting and child online safety programs.
However, parents or guardians would not be penalized for merely failing to supervise their children unless there is proof of willful intent or gross negligence.

Several countries, including Australia, Malaysia, the United Kingdom, and the United Arab Emirates, have introduced age-based restrictions on social media amid concerns over the impact of these platforms on children’s mental health and safety. — VBL, GMA News

articles.title: French minister invites UK to ‘come all the way back’ to the EU
articles.summary:
Finance minister, Roland Lescure, welcomes Burnham’s pledge to explore closer ties with bloc

The French finance minister has invited the UK to “come all the way back” to the European Union…

blocks.text: The French finance minister has invited the UK to “come all the way back” to the European Union after Andy Burnham raised the prospect of a new referendum to reverse Brexit.
Roland Lescure was speaking after the prime minister used his Labour conference speech to pledge that the government would explore closer ties with the bloc at a summit later this year.
He used subsequent interviews to spell out how wide-ranging his consideration of Britain’s future with Brussels could be because Brexit had caused “more harm than good”.

Asked about Burnham’s comments, Lescure told the BBC: “British people decided, and that’s obviously their 100% right, and if they’re willing to come back, they will have to decide. But what I can tell them is: come back, anytime.”
Lescure said he wanted Britain back in the union to face emerging global threats together.

Burnham said last week that the government’s options included keeping the current arrangements in relation to the UK’s relationship with the EU, seeking a customs union, returning to the single market, or going “all the way” with full membership.
He said ministers would examine “what is doable” and the “pros and cons” of each option.

The prime minister is travelling to Germany for talks with the chancellor, Friedrich Merz, whose government has been supportive of Burnham’s suggestion that the UK could explore closer links with the EU.
Burnham and Merz are expected to agree on a deal for closer security cooperation against cyber-attacks on European countries but the two will also discuss UK-EU relations.
Lescure also responded to comments by Burnham that EU rules to help European manufacturers would damage the UK.

British government sources warned days earlier that the “EU reset” summit would be delayed again unless the bloc agreed to discuss legislation that could lock British business out of parts of EU industry.
after newsletter promotion
“Come back, and you’ll be at the table, and we discuss all these things together,” Lescure said.
Nigel Farage has claimed Burnham has given him “the biggest boost in my career” by reviving the Brexit debate, which the Reform UK leader said had reopened a “huge flank” to his party.

Dismissing polls showing that as much as 59% of the public favoured rejoining the EU, Farage said: “Of course they do, until you tell them it’ll cost 25bn quid a year, until you tell him it’ll mean joining Schengen [the area of Europe that has open borders], until he tells them it will mean actually having to recommit to joining the euro.”

articles.title: Christa Pike now walking after US execution went wrong, lawyer tells BBC
articles.summary: A lawyer says the murderer of Colleen Slemmer is moving around her hospital room after surviving two lethal injections.

blocks.text: Christa Pike is "up and walking" while in hospital after last week's botched attempt to execute her in the US state of Tennessee, a member of her legal team says.
Pike, 50, who was sentenced to death after murdering Colleen Slemmer with her then-boyfriend in 1995, survived two lethal injections on 30 September. Experts described it as unprecedented.

Speaking late on Wednesday to BBC Radio 4's Today programme, lawyer Stephen Ferrell said he had not spoken to Pike directly but that he had learned she was moving around her hospital room for the first time while still being mentally "foggy".
Earlier, a court ordered the state of Tennessee to preserve all evidence related to the failed execution.
That evidence could lay the groundwork for a future lawsuit against the state.
The Pike case is now in uncharted territory, as Pike is believed to be the only person to have survived an execution attempt by lethal injection.
The failed execution was branded a "mess" by the mother of Slemmer, who was among those pushing for Pike to be put to death.
Pike's boyfriend at the time of Slemmer's gruesome murder, Tadaryl Shipp, was spared the death penalty because he was not legally an adult when the crime was committed. He remains in prison.
Pike was 18 and Shipp was 17 when they beat, tortured and killed 19-year-old Slemmer, whom they had met at a job training camp for troubled teens.

In their updates on Pike's condition after the attempted execution, her team had previously said she was awake and speaking, and experiencing anger and confusion. She was said at that stage to be handcuffed to her bed.

In the latest updates, given to the BBC, Ferrell said Pike was continuing to experience the after-effects of the drug pentobarbital, which was injected into her body in two doses by prison staff during the scheduled execution on 30 September.
Once it became clear that Pike was not going to die, she was taken to hospital, where she was initially unconscious and declared to have be in a critical condition.
As of late on Tuesday, though, she was "fairly well", Ferrell told the BBC.
"What's been described to me is that physically there's quite a bit going on, that her arms are very injured and she's not able to use them very much."
Of her physical movements, he added: "She is up and walking for the first time today, but just around the room, not very far."

Turning to her mental state, he said: "I think it's kind of good and bad. Good that she is fairly with it, but she's also somewhat foggy. She can lose her train of thought really easily and forgets where she's going."
Ferrell said much remained unknown about what happens next. "I assume [the situation for Pike] will keep improving, but there could be some permanent damage. We don't know that yet."
He added that the team wanted Pike to receive psychological support, since that "clearly is necessary now".

Ferrell and his colleagues - who highlighted ahead of the attempted execution that Pike had a condition that would make the injection method difficult - oppose any new attempt by state prison authorities to follow the same approach.
They are also calling on the state governor, Bill Lee, to downgrade Pike's punishment to the lesser sentence of life in prison without parole.

Meanwhile, Tennessee's proponents of capital punishment have suggested that a different method be used. Senator Marsha Blackburn, the Republican candidate for state governor in next month's election, said: "Bring back the electric chair."
Asked during a court hearing on Wednesday whether the state intended to reschedule Pike's execution, the state's attorney general said he did not know.

For now, Tennessee Governor Bill Lee has ordered a pause on all executions in the state for the rest of the year, and has said he wants answers about what went wrong. The state's prisons chief is resigning after the failed execution.
Wednesday's court hearing related to the preservation of evidence following the first attempt.

The judge, I'Ashea Myles, ordered that "anything that was in the actual room needs to be preserved and maintained," including IV lines and syringes, as well as waste, like packaging, inserts, and labels.
The judge also demanded documentation on Pike's psychological condition prior to, during and after the 30 September execution attempt.
She advised the state to take "special care" not to misplace or accidentally delete any information that may be pertinent to the case.

articles.title: Off the menu: Angel’s Pizza, Figaro Coffee owner set to exit PSE
articles.summary: Fans of Angel’s Pizza and Figaro Coffee need not worry about their favorite snacks disappearing

blocks.text: Composite by Sam Calleja/Rappler
Fans of Angel’s Pizza and Figaro Coffee need not worry about their favorite snacks disappearing

items: Figaro Culinary Group plans to voluntarily delist from the Philippine Stock Exchange less than five years after its debut in January 2022.
The company will offer to buy shares from minority investors at P0.82 each.
The delisting requires shareholder approval and a special meeting is scheduled for November 13 to vote on the proposal.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – The company behind popular Filipino brands Angel’s Pizza and Figaro Coffee is planning an exit from the Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE).

Figaro Culinary Group, which also operates Tien Ma’s Taiwanese Cuisine and Koobideh Kebab, announced on Wednesday, October 7, that its board had approved plans to voluntarily delist from the PSE, less than five years after making its stock market debut in January 2022.

Delisting means the company’s shares would no longer be traded on the exchange. It does not mean the company is shutting down its restaurants, though the investing public will no longer be able to have an ownership stake in the Figaro group.
So what happens to people who invested in Figaro?

Under the tender offer plan, Figaro Coffee Systems, the group’s wholly owned subsidiary that operates its restaurant businesses, will offer to buy shares held by minority investors for P0.82 apiece. (READ: Pizza overtakes coffee in Figaro group’s store footprint as Angel’s Pizza rises)
For comparison, Figaro originally sold shares to the public at P0.75 apiece when it listed in January 2022, raising around P767 million to help fund its expansion.

Monde Nissin, the food manufacturer behind Lucky Me! noodles and SkyFlakes crackers, is among the major shareholders excluded from the proposed buyout. The company acquired a 15% stake in Figaro in 2023 for P820.3 million, equivalent to P1 per share, and is not participating in the P0.82-per-share tender offer alongside two other major shareholders, Carmetheus Holdings and Camerton.

Figaro’s stock market exit is not yet a done deal. Based on the disclosure, the delisting still requires shareholder approval, completion of the tender offer, and Figaro Coffee Systems and the major shareholders collectively reaching at least 95% ownership.
A special stockholders’ meeting is scheduled for November 13 to vote on the proposal.
Trading in Figaro shares was suspended on Thursday, October 8, to give investors time to digest the announcement and assess the offer. – Rappler.com
